citations.review_text: Great game, lousy company that forces their app and launcher on you. Get your bloatware off my PC.

Don't normalize external launchers, stop cluttering my disk with useless crap and horrible broken external launchers.
Just launch my game.

[h3]Rosy Retrospection: The Game™[/h3]

Maybe I’m biased. I started with BF1, moved to BFV, and even survived a love–hate fling with Delta Forc... ahem, 2042, so sure, take this with a grain of salt. But wow, [b]playing this today feels like smearing grease on your glasses and calling it “atmosphere.”[/b] Trust me, I’ve been there.

People don’t remember this game, they remember how it felt back then. Big difference. Nostalgia is doing some Olympic-level heavy lifting here.

This game had its time. That time is not now.

Do yourself a favor, move on to BF6 (Redsec Gauntlet is free!). Or don’t, and keep pretending this still holds up. Your call. 

P.S. Yes, you still have to boot up the EA app to play a game that runs worse than last-gen BF6 on freaking Ultra,  Make it make sense.

Just got done with BF3 story so I had to jump right into Battlefield 4. Overall, I enjoyed it, but I personally liked Battlefield 3 just a little bit more.

The gameplay in 4 definitely feels smoother than BF3, the gunplay is fun, and it's honestly impressive how good this game still looks considering it came out in 2013. The campaign also has some great action moments, and it's easy to see why so many people still play the multiplayer today.

However, the campaign definitely had a lot of issues. I ran into quite a few bugs and glitches, and some of the story choices didn't really make sense. I was so excited to see Dima back only for him to be  killed off shortly after felt unnecessary and didn't add much to the story. I tried the multiplayer for a bit, and it still is as good as I remember it.

The game is definitely worth getting if on sale, it has aged wonderfully!

7/10!

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the single-player campaign features repetitive missions and forgettable characters.

citations.review_text:
This game was my first experience with a Battlefield title when I picked it up back in 2015. Having played most of the other titles, I can confidently say this game is the best of them. There's an immense amount of content available when compared to other titles.

The overall gunplay feels more polished than older titles i.e. BF3, BC2, and lacks the simpler point and shoot mechanics more prevalent in 2042 and BF6. While BF3 has better maps for gameplay I believe that 4 has greater variety especially with the DLCs, i.e. the island-hopping focus of Naval Strike and the futuristic setting in Final Stand.

Another standout about this game is the weapon variety. There are 90 weapons available to unlock with the majority of them not having copy/paste stats. Each class has access to a unique weapon class that leans into the classes' abilities, as well as general weapons available to all four if you prefer a different style. Along with this come with a ton of attachments to choose from to modify how each gun plays.

There are three relatively minor aspects of BF4 I dislike: The campaign, the design of some of the larger maps, and the current price.

The campaign is 4 hours long and has fairly forgettable characters, and has repetitive mission design especially when compared to titles like BF1 and BF3. I don't recommend playing it, although two of the six particularly fun multiplayer weapons (P90 and M249) are locked behind the last mission of the campaign which incentivizes completing it.

The larger maps are really fun to play if you use vehicles, but infantry combat can be pretty frustrating. Golmud Railway, Altai Range, and Silk Road are particular offenders of this, with destructible cover reducing your options to avoid vehicles and have enjoyable gunfights outside of a couple objectives. Previous titles never had maps this big and open, and the games following BF4 largely learned from these missteps.

I'd highly recommend waiting for the sales for this game that come u…

9/10. This is a tough one to review. On paper, Battlefield 4 is arguably a better game than BF3. It has better sandbox mechanics, smoother movement, weapon balance, and a massive array of incredible multiplayer maps with the crazy "Levolution" events. 

But even though it might technically be superior, I can't say for sure if I like it more. Somehow, it just feels slightly less fun than the absolute magic of BF3. 

That being said, it is still an absolute titan of modern military shooters. The multiplayer is an chaotic, explosive sandbox of destruction that still holds up beautifully today. If you want classic, large-scale modern warfare, this is still one of the absolute best options on Steam.

Pros:
+ Massive, diverse map roster with incredible destruction mechanics.
+ High-quality modern gunplay and massive vehicle sandbox.
+ Still has a highly active community.

Cons:
- Single-player campaign is pretty forgettable.
- Somehow misses just a tiny bit of that lightning-in-a-bottle fun factor that BF3 had.

claims.claim: Lobbies and active servers remain available for play.

citations.review_text:
Lobbies are surprisingly active, no matter what time you play, there will always be at least one full US server. Cheating isn’t an issue, server admins aren’t drunk with power, this game is very playable in 2026. The gun-play has aged very well, with only the hit detection feeling a bit outdated, but it’s not frustrating since the enemies bullets are just as likely to phase through you as well.  

Vehicles are on the strong side and not every map is fun to play on, but most are at least interesting to walk through due to the sheer amount of vertical variation. Progression being tied to individual weapons and kits is an amazing idea and I wish more BF games did it. Beyond punk-buster setup, CUAVs, zero audio directionality, and the most toxic in game chat in any online FPS, there’s no reason not to play BF4, it’s an amazing game, it’s an active game, and it’s still pretty casual.
Best modern Battlefield by far, tons of active servers even in 2026, and no BS season pass like BF6.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign mode is poor quality, with some weapon unlocks broken by updates.

citations.review_text:
fun multiplayer (except for AEK sweats and tank farmers)
campaign is mid at best
ery noice

Still one of the best Battlefields ever made. Can still get into a populated match easy, though you need to use the Battlelog server browser to see accurate player numbers (don't need to be logged in to use Battlelog, just to edit your profile/emblem/etc, you can even check your stats, unlocks, rewards, assignments, etc. without logging in by typing in the URL directly, e.g. (...)/bf4/user/<your name here>/, pro tip). It's a benchmark for extremely tight projectile gunplay with a lot of attention to detail and excellent sound design. Weapon customisation is also great, though weapons and attachments can be fairly grindy to unlock since it's based on getting kills and it's a strictly linear progression. Vehicles are powerful but not unstoppable; skillful play is required to do well with them. Just a really well-tuned multiplayer experience overall.

The campaign is pretty terrible, honestly. I'm not sure why they bothered. There are some weapons you can unlock by playing it but last I heard, some update actually broke it so you wouldn't get the unlocks, and it'd been that way for a while. No idea if that's still the case but basically, don't be surprised if it's still broken. The guns aren't anything too special, at least, and there's PLENTY to choose from.

In my opinion, every Battlefield that came after this was worse in some way. It also regularly goes on sale for really, really cheap. Highly recommended.

I got this for $1.99, and it's just not worth the full price in 2026.
Not great for Asia-region players, who are stuck with 200-350 ping.
Only about 5-15 servers are poperly populated, and most will kick for having 150+ ping.
With all that said, getting good games in good maps with "balanced" teams is still possible.
Veterans and sweaty tryhards make up a large portion of the remaining playerbase.
Spending time in "assignment/unlock servers" is a must for getting decent equipment unlocked, or you can spend more $ to skip this. 
Overall, a horrible new player experience, but it gets somewhat tolerable after some grinding. 
Having a buddy or two makes it way more enjoyable.
Check player count in steamdb, don't bother if it's below 1000.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the remaining player base is composed heavily of experienced veterans, resulting in a steep learning curve for newcomers.

citations.review_text:
As someone new to the franchise who started on Battlefield 2042, this is a verry good PvP multiplayer game. I personally consider this the joint best PvP game to play in 2026 alongside Titanfall 2. Some of the great things about this game include:
1. Outside of a few bad apples, the community are generally quite nice and are usually willing to help if you need help getting something.
2. The game (gameplay wise) is in a fairly balanced state and nothing feels absolutely unfair to use.
3. The destruction is in a perfect spot where there isn't too little, nor too much to ruin the game's flow.
however, this game does have a couple of problems to be aware of.
1. This game has been off of support from EA for a long time so cheating is not uncommon.
2. Most of the players here have been playing the game for quite some time and you'll probably lose a lot for your first 100 or so hours.
3. There are microtransactions (battle packs), but they are given out for free and you get plenty of them for just playing the game.

Unironically the best battlefield to date (Yes even better than BF1 imho)

The guns feel amazing, the maps are iconic and fun for the most part. the only genuine issue is just how hard it is to get into the game cus for the most part the people playing this game still to this day are probably vets who has over a decade of experience and hundred's of probably thousands of hours of in game playtime compared to you just starting out.

Being decent at fps games helps but you are still probably going to get absolutely trashed when you first play by sweaty tryhards especially in maps like metro or locker.

Though even with this I still think that if you can push past the starting barrier and get a bit of experience and feel fot he guns and playing and understanding the maps more, this game is such a golden gem its not even funny.

The graphic's while not the most cinematic or the best of the best are serviceable enough to for most people who arnt absolutely anal about games looking uber realistic and that solely being the be all end all of their enjoyment when it comes to games  that they are good enough to not gawk at (at least for modern standards) and not terrible enough to make any real complaints, its over a decade old and for the time period of this games existence they looked quite amazing but nowadays they are just fine at best.

My first exposure to this legendary franchise was bf3 on my old ps3 in 2012. Played that game to oblivion but around 2014, I left abroad for my university and didn't have a console for gaming. That is the same year when this game was released. So I saw the trailers, the reviews, the outrage on the buggy launch but never had the time to try it.

Fast forward to 2024 when this was on sale and it came up on my steam recommendations. Given how cheap it was... I bought it and, after so many years, I stepped into the world of Battlefield.

Immediately I had a ratatouille moment. A deja vu to my child hood and I started playing this game. It is a testament how this game has aged like fine win in all departments (except the single player, which wasn't great to begin with).
The graphics, the colors, the art style, the gameplay, the destruction, the maps, the mapflow, all 10/10.

I can easily sink 100s of hours into this game. Each game is so much fun. Yes the player base that's left are all experts but man, the game provides a battlefield experience like no other.

An easy 10/10. 
The maps in this game are what the team behind bf6 should look at when designing new maps. 
May mersonal favourites are in no particular order:
Zavod 311, Siege of Shanghai, Paracel Storm, Hainan Resort, Dawn breaker, Operation Locker,  Golmud Railway, Caspian Border, Operation Firestorm, Operation Metro, Guilin Peaks, Pearl Market, Propoganda, Hangar 21.
